It's worth noting that baking soda is a buffer solution, not a base or an acid. It can act like one in the presence of the other, which is why baking soda works with vinegar, but by default it's not trying to force a reaction. This means it will try to moderate the pH, while boric acid will instead be trying to react with things.

Boric acid also has a pH of 9.33 at its first protonation point, which is fairly acidic.

My guess is that they (A) didn't mix the proper ratios, which left some borax left over in the slime, and (B) made the slime at full concentration instead of diluting the glue down in water, which would have helped rinse away the borax.
